newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Oct 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Oct 28.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Bangladesh may ask for 35,000 to 40,000 cusecs of water during the lean period as Dhaka and Delhi resume talks on sharing of Ganges flow on Tuesday in the Indian capital.
Opposition leader Begum Khaleda Zia has urged the ruling party to ensure the "right to speak" of the opposition in the parliament's next session beginning Friday.
The government plans to hold peace talks with tribal Shantibahini insurgents in hill districts sometime in late November.
Opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has criticised Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina for what it said was not raising Ganges water issue in her speech at the United Nations last week.
Loading and unloading in southern Mongla Port were seriously disrupted on Sunday due to inclement weather and incessant rainfall caused by depression in the Bay of Bengal.

Societe Generale, one of the largest French banks, opens a branch in Dhaka on Monday, focusing France's growing interest in developing business with Bangladesh. Banque Nationale de Paris, another top French bank, is expected to open branch in Dhaka next year.
